record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.context_brief: Borel realizability of centers of distances
record.original_question: If A ⊂ [0,∞) is a Borel set containing 0, must there exist a Borel set B ⊂ ℝ whose center of distances C(B) equals A? Here C(B) = {α ≥ 0 : for every x in B there exists y in B with d(x,y)=α}.

evidence.page: Section 7, definition of center of distances
evidence.quote: C(A) := {α ≥ 0 : ∀x ∈ A, ∃y ∈ A with d(x, y) = α}.
Is it true that for any Borel set 0 ∈ A ⊂ [0,∞), there exists a Borel set B ⊆ R with C(B) = A?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a nonempty subset $A$ of a metric space $(X,d)$, define the center of distances of $A$ by
$$C(A) := \{\alpha \geq 0 : \text{for every } x \in A \text{ there exists } y \in A \text{ with } d(x,y) = \alpha\}.$$
Consider $\mathbb{R}$ with the standard Euclidean metric. 

Question: Is it true that for every Borel set $A \subseteq [0,\infty)$ with $0 \in A$, there exists a Borel set $B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ such that $C(B) = A$?
artifact.category_tag: centers of distances and achievement sets
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on achievement sets and centers of distances. A web search did not reveal any published resolution; related work has characterized centers of distances in particular cases (e.g., for achievement sets of series, Cantorvals) but the general Borel realizability question for subsets of $[0,\infty)$ containing $0$ appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Achievement sets of series in R^2
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses centers of distances and the spectre as a generalization, with results about which sets can be centers of distances.
status_evidence.claim: Related research on centers of distances exists but does not resolve the general Borel realizability question.
